A balmy early summer evening -
N | I'm sitting on our terrace after work,
scrolling through photos on my
mobile. When I reach the month of
| June in the year 2024, it suddenly
; gets loud. Videos of roaring GT3
racing cars winding their way up the
Eau Rouge appear on the screen.
4“ Goosebumps... Longing...
| think for a moment and then ask
Google when this year’s Spa-Fran-
corchamps 24-hour race is taking
place. After a quick check of the
calendar, I’m delighted to realise:
there’s no appointment on that
particular weekend yet.
I quickly check the availability of tickets and then call out to my wife:
“Darling! Carlo and | are off to Belgium for a weekend in June!”
Carlo is the older of my
two sons, four years old
and a huge motorsport
fan for at least three
and a half years. | pro-
bably don’t need to ex- Saaaame
plain here where his in-
terest in loud and fast
cars comes from.
A few weeks later, we’re |
off. We’ve got at least a |
five-hour drive ahead of |
us.

The trunk is packed full with a
handcart, plenty of spare T-shirts,
lots of water and even more sun
cream. It’s set to be very hot in the
Ardennes.
After a more or less pleasant
journey in the air-conditioned car,
we finally reach the race track. As
we open the doors, we’re hit by a
wave of heat. It’s supposed to be 38
degrees, but it feels more like 45.
We slap on some sun cream and
finally set off with the covered handcart towards the grandstand above
Eau Rouge. We arrive there just in time for the start of the Superpole. The
GT3 cars are circling their way up the tarmac strip. One after the other,
sometimes several at once.
| look contentedly at my
son, who is sitting next
tome wearingacapand 7
noise protection, trying &
to catch a glimpse of
the cars thundering past
through his binoculars.
And despite the 38°
outside temperature,
| realise they‘re back -
the goosebumps.
